name: RV Camping Checklist
description: A complete RV camping checklist covering departure prep, hookups and setup, kitchen and living supplies, and breaking camp.

items.text: Check tire pressure on the RV and tow vehicle
Inspect the hitch, brakes, and safety chains
Fill the fresh water tank and empty waste tanks
Top off fuel and propane
Test running lights, brake lights, and turn signals
Check the weather and road conditions for your route
items.note: Watch for low clearances and weight-restricted roads.

items.text: Plan stops and confirm your campsite reservation
Surge protector and shore power cord
Electrical adapters (30/50 amp)
Drinking-water-safe hose and a backup
Water pressure regulator and inline filter
Sewer hose, fittings, and disposable gloves
Tank treatment chemicals
Leveling blocks and a bubble level
Wheel chocks
Stabilizer jack pads
Awning and outdoor mat
Camp chairs and an outdoor table
Position and level the rig, then connect power, water, and sewer in order
Pots, pans, and cooking utensils
Plates, bowls, cups, and cutlery
Coffee maker and a kettle
Food, snacks, and drinks for the trip
Dish soap, sponge, and dish towels
Trash bags and storage containers
Secure cabinets and the fridge before driving
Bedding, pillows, and blankets
Towels and toiletries
Weather-appropriate clothing and shoes
First-aid kit and medications
Fans or a portable heater for comfort
Entertainment: books, games, downloaded shows
Basic tool kit and duct tape
Flashlight, headlamp, and spare batteries
Fire extinguisher and smoke and CO detectors
Roadside emergency kit and warning triangles
Spare fuses, bulbs, and a tire repair kit
Work gloves and a small broom
Empty and flush the waste tanks
Disconnect and stow all hookups
Retract the awning, slides, and stabilizers
Secure loose items and latch cabinets
Raise the steps and chock-free the wheels
Do a final walk-around before pulling out
items.note: Confirm hookups are stowed and the hitch is locked.

faq.q: What do I need for RV camping?
faq.a: You need hookup gear like a drinking-water hose, sewer hose, and a surge-protected power cord, plus leveling blocks, wheel chocks, and your usual camping supplies. Add a stocked galley, bedding, and tools for both campsite setup and travel days.

faq.q: How do I set up an RV at a campsite?
faq.a: Position and level the RV, chock the wheels, then connect power, water, and sewer in that order. Extend the awning and slides, set up outdoor gear, and test that systems are working before you settle in.

Hookups are the campsite connections for electricity, fresh water, and sewer waste. A full-hookup site offers all three; partial sites may have only power and water, so carry your fresh tank and check what each site provides.

faq.q: Can I print this RV camping checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item during departure prep, campsite setup, and breaking camp.

faq.q: What should I check before driving the RV?
faq.a: Before each travel day, secure loose items, retract slides and the awning, disconnect hookups, check tire pressure and lights, confirm the hitch is locked, and walk around the rig. Check the weather and road conditions on your route.
